as_told.title: Green fireballs around atmospheric nuclear tests
as_told.place_text: New Mexico, US nuclear test sites

plain: In 1948, Michels says, Lincoln LaPaz, a meteor expert at the University of New Mexico, began studying green fireballs that kept showing up near nuclear facilities and detonations. Michels tells it more than once without naming a source. In one telling he credits the researcher Robert Hastings' book UFOs and Nukes, ties the fireballs to atmospheric bomb tests, calls them "intelligently moving", and says they were also documented by Edward J. Ruppelt, then head of Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. If true, it would suggest something was taking an interest in America's first nuclear sites.
